correctness.rationale: Det(lambda I-Q)=lambda(lambda²+S lambda+T), with Δ=S²−4T=−(u+v+w)(−u+v+w)(u−v+w)(u+v−w) for square-root rates. For Δ>0 decreasing unique too-large u to v+w raises the gap while lowering cost, so no positive optimum outside the triangle domain. Inside Γ=S/2 and cost ratio is quadratic Rayleigh quotient. For unequal prices the cheapest coordinate grows to a triangle facet u=v+w; 2x2 generalized eigenvalue equation yields Λ=3/(P−δ). Perron positivity gives unique interior facet if least price strictly unique; tie cases produce boundary nonattainment or all-price continuum. Repeated nonzero eigenvalues cannot be diagonalizable in irreducible one-way Q because that would force every off-diagonal positive. Independent 6 specific price triples' generator eigenvalues match the formula. All-real parameter result rests on analytical argument.

value.rationale: Complete analytic solution of smallest genuinely directed nonreversible mixing design with cost asymmetry, sharp distinction between attained and unattained optimum and a defective eigenvalue mechanism. It explicitly separates asymptotic exponent from finite-time mixing, making a useful benchmark.

final_claim: For a 3-state one-way CTMC with positive rates x,y,z, positive prices p1,p2,p3 and budget B, optimal nonzero spectral decay exponent has supremum Γ*=3B/[2(P-δ)] where P=sum prices, δ=sqrt(sum p_i^2 - sum pair products). Unique cheapest price gives unique irreducible optimum at repeated nonzero defective eigenvalues; two cheapest tied below third gives unattained supremum, equal prices a continuum of optimal square-root triangle triples.
